patterns: Short cryptic hook + strong clip wins the day: EHuanglu's 'AI just created a new way to tell story' hit 139.2K views, 1,753 likes and 1,071 bookmarks (bookmarks at ~61% of likes = people save it to study).

Hollywood-director workflows are the new authority content: CharaspowerAI quoting Jon Erwin's AI-assisted Seedance 2.5 workflow reached 91.6K views (low likes, 31, so reach came from the quoted video), EHuanglu's 'the gap got smaller' reflection 22.6K, azed_ai's 'the real performance remains at the center' 10.6K. Outside the watchlist, shedntcare_'s 'keyframes first, then Seedance' got 41.5K.

MiniMax H3 Image vs Seedream 5.5 side-by-sides flood the outsider lane (Aria_Nawi 533.3K, nrqa__ 247.9K, jessibuilds 125.4K, VibeEverything 92.3K with 853 bookmarks); much of it looks like a launch push. On the watchlist, AIWarper's practical H3 tips (80MP on a 4090/5090, run at 20-40MP) got 10.3K with more bookmarks (173) than likes (157).
The 'famous IP, but it's 197x' format is cooling: techhalla's Stranger Things 1972 did 31.3K vs 134.5K for The Avengers 1972 the day before.
minchoi stays on the board with news recaps (Seedream 5.5 drop 19.5K, Jensen Huang posts 12.9K-14.6K, Claude Meetings 10.2K) and a funny AI cat video (29.9K).

drafts.draft_en:
Jon Erwin just shared his AI-assisted filmmaking workflow with Seedance 2.5.

After House of David S2, here's what I'd tell any director starting today:

AI doesn't replace the shot list. It makes it visible. 👇
drafts.video_tip: 15-20s split screen: storyboard/shot-list frame on the left, final AI VFX shot on the right, 3-4 shots back to back with a SHOT 01/02/03 label. Put the 4-step workflow in the first reply.

drafts.draft_en:
AI just gave VFX a new way to tell a story.

One frame in. One scene out. 🎬
drafts.video_tip: 8-12s: open on the single still for 1s, then a seamless push-in that becomes a moving scene; no text overlay, let the clip carry the hook. Loop-friendly last frame = first frame.

drafts.draft_en:
MiniMax H3 Image vs Seedream 5.5.

Same VFX plate prompt.

Which one would you put in a film? 1 or 2 👇
drafts.video_tip: Two stills side by side, or a 6s wipe between them on a beat; label 1 and 2 only (no model names on the image) to drive replies. Drop the prompt in the reply.

drafts.draft_en:
Keyframes first. Motion second.

I locked character, costume and blocking in stills, then let Seedance 2.5 animate.

Here's the breakdown 👇
drafts.video_tip: 10-15s: grid of 4 locked keyframes for 2s, then each one animates in sequence into the final cut. Reply with the keyframe prompts.

drafts.draft_en:
Saturday Challenge 🎞️

This week: a 10-second scene where the performance carries it, not the effects.

Post yours below. I'll break down my top 3 next week.
drafts.video_tip: 6-8s teaser: close-up of a face with a subtle emotional shift, then a 'SATURDAY CHALLENGE' title card. Pin it for the weekend.
